reasoning.text: The render reads clearly as an FPGA accelerator card: dark PCB, gold PCIe fingers, twin HBM stacks, heatsink under an exploded blue floorplan plate whose logic blocks are all visible from above (good X-ray). The one substantive faithfulness gap is the carried-over v2 delta — the twiddle ROM is still modelled as the full 1023-word block that dominates the floorplan, and the psi-fold (fold7) derive-gate that halves it is absent, so the scene depicts v1 rather than the shipped CFNTT-KRED v2. Secondary weaknesses: the heatsink fin stack and most logic blocks are plain boxes (geometry axis), and the thin copper datapath/PWM spines are barely legible in the render.
gaps: Geometric fidelity: the heatsink fin stack and several logic blocks are plain boxes; consider a shallow finned silhouette for the heatsink (still ONE part) and slightly varied footprints so the pipeline stages read as distinct hardware, not a row of identical cubes.
The copper datapath_bus and pwm_feedback spines are nearly invisible in the render — raise them slightly above the plate or widen them so the operand routing is legible from ISO.

Consider showing the 4-stage K-RED pipeline depth more literally (the single 14x14 multiplier visibly larger/brass vs the two shift-add fold stages) so a viewer counts one multiplier + two folds + one csub at a glance.

fields.before: Single shared 1023-word twiddle ROM storing W = 9^-1·w so that 9·v·W = v·w exactly in the NTT butterfly — no post-multiply correction needed; taller footprint signals its word depth vs the small registers.
fields.after: Shared 512-word twiddle ROM storing ONLY the 9^-1-scaled lower half of W (addresses 1..512); the psi-folded upper half (w_rom[512+j] = 7*w_rom[j] mod q) is NOT stored but reconstructed by the tf_fold7 gate on its output — was the largest block on the floorplan, now half the footprint.

before.notes: Layout/size identical to reference tf_ROM; the 9^-1 pre-scaling is what makes the factor 9 from K-RED disappear architecturally.

params.word_stores: 9^-1-scaled lower half of W (9^-1 = 2731 mod q); addresses = w_rom[1..512]
params.psi: kesai = 7; upper half w_rom[512+j] = 7*w_rom[j] mod q
params.replaces: tf_ROM.v (1023 words) with tf_rom_fold.v, same interface, 1-cycle latency

after.notes: v2 psi-fold: only the lower half is stored; the upper half derives via tf_fold7. Measured 7828 -> 1611 cells (-79%), stored bits 14322 -> 7168 (-50%). Formally verified equivalent to the shipped tf_ROM.v at every address (SymbiYosys miter, 9*Q_new == Q_ref mod q).

fields.before: Two-stage delay of the twiddle W read from ROM, aligning it to the multiplier's B input; longer in Z to show the w_q1→w_q2 pipeline depth.
fields.after: Two-stage delay of the folded twiddle W coming off the tf_fold7 gate, aligning it to the multiplier's B input; longer in Z to show the w_q1→w_q2 pipeline depth.

before.notes: w --DFF--> w_q1 --DFF--> w_q2 in compact_bf_v2; then modular_half feeds the sel mux.

after.notes: w --DFF--> w_q1 --DFF--> w_q2 in compact_bf_v2; fed by the half-size ROM through tf_fold7, then modular_half feeds the sel mux.

before.notes: One of the two op21 gates that fix reference issue #7; fuses the per-stage INTT halving into the twiddle derivation.

after.notes: One of the two op21 gates that fix reference issue #7; fuses the per-stage INTT halving into the twiddle derivation. Sits alongside tf_fold7 on the ROM output path.

fields.before: The ONLY hardware multiplier in the butterfly: a 14×14→28-bit product z = A·B (the reference Barrett unit spent three multipliers); also re-driven by the PWM return bus for the double-pass mode.
fields.after: The ONLY hardware multiplier in the butterfly: a 14×14→28-bit product z = A·B (the reference Barrett unit spent three multipliers); deliberately the largest brass block so the single-DSP core reads at a glance; also re-driven by the PWM return bus for the double-pass mode.

meta.before: Root everything on the PCB. Populate the board: a gold PCIe edge connector, the FPGA BGA package carrying the exposed silicon die, an in-package HBM stack on each side, a clock oscillator, two bulk decoupling caps and an auxiliary power tap; a brushed-steel cold plate and its finned stack cap the die. From the four die corners, four thin brushed-steel standoff risers (clear of the heatsink footprint) lift an exploded logic-floorplan plate directly above the die; the plate carries the synthesized CFNTT-KRED butterfly datapath (compact_bf_v2). Two conflict-free memory banks (white composite) with their address generators stream u/v coefficients into input DFFs, while a single shared 1023-word twiddle ROM (black composite, storing W = 9^-1·w) feeds the w delay chain. Before the multiplier two selects sit: v_mux picks the A operand (v for NTT, v−u for INTT) and the NTT/INTT mux picks the B operand (W or op21(W)). The K-RED modular multiplier is a 4-stage pipeline — ONE 14×14→28 hardware multiplier (brass), then two shift-add fold stages (d = 3z+6q−z>>12; e = 3d+q−d>>12) and one conditional subtraction — producing 9·A·B mod q. A modular_add combines u with the product; two modular_half (op21) copper gates, one on the ROM output and one on the add path, derive the per-stage INTT halving that fixes the reference's 2^10-scaling bug, with add_mux selecting the halved sum onto the bank writeback during INTT. A copper PWM return bus feeds the K-RED result back into v_mux for the double-pass mode. A control FSM sequences the banks, ROM addresses, both muxes and the sel line; a copper datapath bus threads the stages.

        "description": "The NTT is a finite-field analogue of the FFT that turns O(n^2) polynomial multiplication in Z_q[x]/(x^n+1) into O(n log n) butterfly passes; it is the throughput bottleneck of schemes like Kyber, NewHope and Dilithium. This design maps a bank of Cooley–Tukey/Gentleman–Sande butterfly processing elements onto the FPGA fabric, streaming coefficients from on-package HBM and reading twiddle factors from a ROM.
